content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble reading a value from my smart-me module. I can see the value in my Modbus test program, but I can't figure out how to get it into my [product_name] program. Please see the attached files below. I would appreciate it if someone could review this. Thanks!
Are you trying to read a value with [product_name]? If so, is the issue that the value isn't what you expect?
Try reading more registers in sequence. If all are zero, there may be no communication.
You're reading two registers at the address, but only one register with the usual NAI. Double register values have 4 bytes, but you're only reading the left two bytes.
Sorry, I don't understand. Should I enter more values in the Data Transfer list or add more NAI? Can you show me an example in a program?
The way you're setting it up doesn't make sense—there's an overlap.
Exactly—use the data table and take a screenshot like this.
Do you see what I'm doing wrong?
No. Please follow my suggestion in the previous post.
Thank you! Now I understand, but there’s still no progress—only zero values. Is there a way to check if communication between [product_name] and the module is working correctly?
If you’ve taken a screenshot during Online-Test of [product_name], then it seems like there’s no connection between [product_name] and the smart-me module.

Hi, the register you're trying to read is a DWord. When you're in online test, open the data table and add VD0. [product_name] only supports signed integer, not the DWord data format. Hope this helps.
[product_name] does not support DInt, but it does handle float (32 bit) with the F/I converter.

The first issue is an incorrect IP address in your [product_name] program for the Modbus server. It should be 192.168.0.121 (QModMaster), but in [product_name] you have 198.168.0.121. The second issue might be the data type. [product_name] only recognizes 16-bit signed integers (-32768 to +32767). Your values use 4 bytes = 32-bit signed or unsigned integer. Look for float values in the Modbus table; these can be converted in [product_name] to 16-bit signed integer, but you might lose some decimals. Regards, [user_name]

You're correct: [product_name] only supports signed integer. If you read or write a DW or Float to [product_name]'s V-Memory (via ModbusTCP or S7), you can see it in the Online test data table. Open the table and add VDx; you can also view float values. The memory in [product_name] can be used to forward such values to AWS, [company_name], etc. But [product_name] cannot use values outside the signed integer range in the program, except for F/I and I/F instructions, which simply transfer unsupported data formats into signed integer.
Thank you all for the assistance! No solution yet, but I'll find more time to continue the project.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulty integrating a smart-me module with [product_name] via Modbus. While the target value appears in a Modbus test program, it fails to be retrieved by the [product_name] system, resulting in only zero values. The challenge seems related to improper register reading settings—notably on the number of registers read and data mapping—causing overlap or incomplete data retrieval. Troubleshooting communication and more precise mapping strategies are at the core of the issue.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to accurately display the correct value from the smart-me module, as it appears in the Modbus test program, with minimal troubleshooting and without a complicated setup.
